key_insight: Placing a pretrained LLM inside a sandboxed virtual computer enables it to autonomously use computing tools (file system, scripts, external resources) to solve non-code tasks, revealing agentic general intelligence without extra training.
problem_solved: Overcomes limitations of static LLM outputs by giving models a safe, programmable environment to retrieve knowledge, manage very long contexts, and automate multi-step formatting or processing—without fine-tuning.
method: Run an off-the-shelf LLM with access to a code sandbox that exposes a shell, file system, and controlled network/resource interfaces.
Let the LLM generate and execute scripts, read/write files, and fetch external data to extend memory, perform computations, and satisfy task constraints.
Evaluate emergent behaviors on non-code tasks (knowledge acquisition, long-context handling, formatting automation) to demonstrate generalization.
impact: Practical pathway to turn pretrained LLMs into capable, self-directed agents for complex workflows—improving flexibility, reproducibility, and real-world utility without additional model training.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: LLM connected to sandbox components (shell, file system, network) with arrows showing read/write/execute actions.
Flowchart example: non-code task solved step-by-step (fetch data → write file → run script → produce final answer).
Before/After timeline: handling a long document via direct prompt vs. segmented file-system-assisted processing.
Bar or radar chart: emergent capabilities (knowledge retrieval, context length, automation, formatting) comparing baseline LLM vs LLM-in-Sandbox.
paper_authors: Daixuan Cheng, Shaohan Huang, Yuxian Gu, Huatong Song, Guoxin Chen
